## TL;DR

Close-out validations now overlap across runner slots, while publishing stays strictly serial in queue order. This session fixed the handoff failure (three test files failed because a config save called a pump callback that their fixtures never supplied), verified each open review finding against the current code, and closed the two coverage gaps the review found: same-millisecond queue order and a live parallel-limit save waking the pump. The scoped `repoos check` result is recorded below.

## Work and rationale

The feature itself was already committed on this branch: a `CloseOutScheduler` (`src/server/close-out-scheduler.ts`) that calls `selectCloseOutStarts` in `src/server/integration-job.ts`, a `maxParallelValidations` setting (default 2, 1 to 8, live Settings select), and a publish turn so only the head of the queue merges. This session started from the queued handoff failure and the second review.

The handoff failure was one root cause. `patchConfig` calls `ctx.triggerJobProcessing()` after every save, which is correct for the real server but absent from the test contexts in `activity-animation-size-config`, `allowlist-groups` and `areas-settings`. Twelve tests failed with `ctx.triggerJobProcessing is not a function`. I considered making the callback optional, but the route type declares it required and the server always supplies it, so an optional call would hide a real wiring gap. Instead the route now pumps only when the saved `maxParallelValidations` differs from its value before the reload. That is what the review asked for (a raised limit must start queued work now), it keeps unrelated saves quiet, and it is the same before/after pattern the area-vocabulary drift check already uses. I applied it to the raw `repoos.toml` write path too, since that path also reloads config. All 53 tests in the three files pass.

I then checked each review finding against the current code rather than the reviewed tree, since the implementation commit landed after the second review:

- Timeout budget: the budget now restarts only when a run begins in the `publishing` phase, which happens only after a parked wait. A publish-time drift returns the job to `syncing`, so a drift cannot reset the budget again within one run.
- Scheduler liveness: a publishing head takes no validation slot and is not held by the pressure guard, so a slow validation cannot block its own publish.
- Queue ordering: enqueue stamps are strictly increasing, and `allJobs` breaks any tie by task id. I added a test that enqueues four jobs back to back and checks both the order and the stamps.
- Pipeline UI: `integrationPipelineStalled` exempts a publisher parked for its turn, and `closeOutFailureCutoff` reads a parallel job's own start, so failure cutoffs no longer drift with snapshot time. Callers in `TaskCard.vue` and `PipelineView.vue` pass the task id.
- Accessibility: the parallel-job chip in `IntegrationStatusBar.vue` now uses `aria-label` instead of a native `title`.
- Test coverage: `close-out-scheduler.test.ts` drives the live pump with gated fake runs and covers overlap up to the limit, slot reuse, publish order, failure isolation, the pressure hold and the parked head.

I added `src/ui-app/tests/close-out-parallel-config-wake.test.ts`, which checks that a raised limit wakes the pump exactly once and that an unchanged limit does not.

## Approaches tried

I first ran the three failing files with `bunx vitest`. That resolved to a `dist/` under the main checkout, so I stopped that run by PID and used `bun run test:vitest` for UI-config tests and the local `node_modules/.bin/vitest` for the server tests. I did not touch the main checkout's files.

For the timeout-budget finding I considered resetting the budget only when a job is re-parked. The current guard, which keys on the phase a run starts in, is smaller and already fits the drift path, so I kept it and relied on the existing parked-publisher tests rather than adding another harness.

## Challenges and blockers

The review's accessibility finding names `IntegrationStatusBar.vue:679`. That line is now the parallel chip. Other `title` attributes in the same file, on the queue chips and the collapse button, predate this branch and are not part of this change, so I left them. Filing them as a separate accessibility task would keep this diff scoped.

I did not capture the declared shots myself. The task declares a `/checks?tab=now` pipeline state and a `/settings` config row; RepoOS captures them at handoff from the managed preview.

## Key learnings

A required route dependency is only safe if every test fixture provides it. The failures were a fixture gap, not a logic bug, but the real route was correct to call the pump. Gating the call on the value that changed fixes the fixtures without weakening the server path.

Review findings can refer to a tree that a later commit already changed. Checking each one against the current code before editing avoided rewriting fixes that were already in place.
